_comment_consumer: `README.md` does not fnmatch `tools/README.md`, so the catalogue needs its own glob and adding `tools` to `include` alone buys it no figure coverage at all. Measured 2026-08-10: a false four-decimal ratio and a false cent-precise spend planted in `tools/README.md` produce zero firings under the `include` widening alone and two errors once `tools/*.md` is a consumer.
_comment_search_roots: Where a figure or an identifier may be *found* even if it is not authoritative. Used to say 'appears nowhere else in the corpus', which is the strongest transcription-error signal. Extensions here are wider than the document extensions above because committed harness results are JSON and text.
_comment_numeric: Digit strings that are legitimately not measurements. Each needs a reason. Prefer narrowing a pattern over adding entries here.
_comment_kinds: Which figure shapes the provenance check extracts. Four-decimal ratios are this corpus's house style for a measured rate and are close to noise-free; multipliers and money-with-cents are nearly as good. `percent_decimal` and `fraction` are implemented and OFF by default: research/01, /04, /05 and /13 survey external systems and quote dozens of vendor and paper percentages that are legitimately not our measurements, and turning them on produces roughly 125 violations of which almost none are actionable. Turn them on for a targeted sweep of one document, not for the gate.
_comment_identifiers: Identifier namespaces to resolve. Discovered by reading the registers in research/14-architecture-synthesis.md, the owner decisions in specs/001-discovery-validation/plan.md, and the requirements in each feature's own specs/*/spec.md. A namespace is only enforced if the corpus defines at least `min_definitions` members of it, so a namespace that stops existing turns the check off rather than producing noise. `what` is an EMITTED surface, not a comment: it is interpolated into five operator-facing strings — four in checks/identifiers.py, being the disabled skip line, the partly-read skip line, an `identifier-resolution` violation's `expected`, and an `identifier-gap` violation's `found`, plus a `definition-count` hint in checks/definition_counts.py. ~~The `path` field is the one that settles the wording: every other violation prints a real relpath in that column, so this string stands where a file the reader can open belongs.~~ **The fourth site was `identifier-gap`'s `path` field until 2026-08-12 and is now its `found`.** That field is why these strings had to read as addresses at all, and it no longer does: `identifier-gap` computes its `path` from where this run's corpus actually defines the namespace, which is what makes it correct in the two fixture trees as well as this one. The addressing requirement on these strings is therefore RELAXED, not removed — all four remaining sites are prose, so a label naming a shape a reader can find is still worth more than a bare noun, and none of them is a column anybody tries to open. The strings are left exactly as the 2026-08-12 rebuild wrote them, because the census that produced them also corrected three of the four about the register's SHAPE, and that half of the work is unaffected by where the fourth site prints. Four of the nine named a bare basename until 2026-08-12: `plan.md` and `spec.md` each fnmatch two features, there is no file of either name at the repository root, and the shared-basename trap in tools/README.md is what that costs. The strings were rebuilt from a census taken with this tool's own `definitions_in` rather than by grep, and cross-checked against the counts the partly-read skip line prints. Three of the four were also wrong about the register's SHAPE, not merely its address. `FR` and `SC` are plural and their tokens COLLIDE: specs/001-discovery-validation/spec.md defines FR-001..FR-022 and SC-001..SC-009, specs/002-spec-aware-agent-runtime/spec.md defines FR-001..FR-058 and SC-001..SC-030, the two FR-001s are different requirements, and `_collect_definitions` unions them by token, so a dangling FR in one feature can still resolve against the other's register — `definition-count` already reads these per feature via `definition_count_target`, and only this label said `spec.md` as though there were one. `E` is plural too: 15 of its 19 members are the ladder in specs/001-discovery-validation/plan.md and E16..E19 are each defined by their own harness index, which is what OD-31 in that same plan.md records. The old string was self-refuting in its own message — narrowing to the very plan.md it named printed `4 of 19 definition(s) are outside the --path selection, so the register (experiment ladder, plan.md) was only partly read`. `D`, `P`, `O`, `C` and `U` were left alone deliberately: `research/14` is directory-scoped house shorthand used at 130 sites, research/ holds exactly one `14-*` file, and each carries a section anchor a bare path would lose — they are shorthand that resolves, not a basename that forks. No range or count is written into any of these strings, because nothing checks one and it would be a fresh unguarded claim in an emitted line. These stay HAND-WRITTEN rather than being derived from a namespace-to-owning-document map, and the reason is measured, not stylistic: asking which single document defines a namespace's whole union names one for eight of the nine, and for `FR` and `SC` it names specs/002-spec-aware-agent-runtime/spec.md — wrongly, because 001's FR-001..FR-022 are a token subset of 002's FR-001..FR-058 while meaning different requirements. A derived label would therefore erase feature 001's register and look verified doing it. `E` is the only namespace whose plurality that test can see, since no one document covers its union. Derivation would move the rot rather than remove it.

FR.what: functional requirements, one register per feature at specs/*/spec.md

SC.what: success criteria, one register per feature at specs/*/spec.md

E.what: experiment ladder, specs/001-discovery-validation/plan.md; non-ladder experiments at their own harness index

_comment_dry_run: A run directory that declares `dry_run: true` called no model, so anything in it that reads as an outcome was computed against stub output. `roots` are globs for run directories; a directory is only scanned if one of its own JSON files declares the marker, so the harness decides what counts as a dry run and this check inherits it. Exemption is deliberately LINE-LOCAL: the artifacts that produced this rule already disclosed the stub in a banner at the top of a different file, which is exactly what a grep does not read. `case_sensitive` exists for one reason — `verdict` is a field name in every judge-call row in the corpus, so the labelled-verdict rule matches upper case only.

verdict_patterns.name: gate-outcome
verdict_patterns.why: a gate outcome is the decision itself, and every gate in this harness reads a metric defined over judge verdicts

verdict_patterns.name: gate-state
verdict_patterns.why: same decision stated with the gate as subject

verdict_patterns.name: hypothesis-outcome
verdict_patterns.why: a hypothesis verdict; the experiment ladder's hypotheses are exactly what a stub run cannot speak to

verdict_patterns.name: product-promotion
verdict_patterns.why: promotes a measurement to a product decision, which is a scope call and not a number

verdict_patterns.name: labelled-verdict
verdict_patterns.why: an explicitly labelled outcome; upper case only, because `verdict` is a field name in every judge-call and oracle row

verdict_patterns.name: superiority
verdict_patterns.why: a comparative verdict; E19's own target for the verifier is the phrase 'materially better'

verdict_patterns.name: significance
verdict_patterns.why: an inferential claim, which no stub-scored sample supports

dry_run._comment_disclosure: Tokens that make the line self-describing. Lower-cased substring match, checked against the raw line before masking.
dry_run._comment_prohibition: Tokens marking a line that forbids the claim rather than making it. Separate from disclosure because the reason differs: the line is honest about the rule, not about the artifact.

_comment_inventory: Prose claims about how many of a thing the repository contains. Each rule is a regex whose one capture group is the claimed count, plus a glob whose match count is the truth. `files` scopes the rule: an inventory claim belongs in an index document, and the same words elsewhere almost always mean something else — 'Three findings converge on X' is a sentence about conclusions, not a count of documents, and scanning the whole corpus for it produced eleven false positives against two real ones.

inventory_rules._comment: This rule read nothing from its creation until 2026-08-11, established by replaying it against this check's own masking over all 14 revisions of the two documents in its default scope rather than by reading its history: it matched in none of them. `README.md` and `research/README.md` carry seven revisions each. An earlier form of this sentence read 266, which is the repository's total commit count at `c9e42ad` and a revision count of nothing — a commit count relabelled, with its operands never stated. The conclusion is untouched by the correction and is now checkable: zero live matches before `451725f`, one at it, and that one agrees. That site is `README.md`'s repository-map cell, which states the corpus-wide total across both `findings/` directories — the scope this glob actually spans, and the reason the claim belongs in a corpus-wide document rather than in either feature's index. `files` is left at the default rather than widened, and both candidate widenings were measured before the choice. Each cost below is a dated count over a named tree rather than a standing property, because nothing recomputes either one. Whole-corpus `files` fires 26 times at `e551a29` on 2026-08-11, against 23 when it was first measured at `7d723c1`, on prose of the shape `Three findings converge on X`, with zero real defects — the same disposition as the `unconstructib*` candidate under *What this cannot catch*, declined on numbers. Widening `files` to `specs/*/findings/README.md` fires 3 times at `e551a29`, against once at `7d723c1`: both indexes' own H1s parse as counts, `Feature 001 findings` as `1` and `Feature 002 findings` as `2`, and feature 001's index states a count over its own directory that parses as `19` — all three against an actual of 37. The figure moved because feature 001's index was created at `d590ac0`, after the first measurement, so the earlier `fires once and permanently` was right about the count on the day it was taken and wrong about the permanence: this declination's cost grows with every index the corpus adds. Both scope changes cost a false positive and buy no site the repository map does not already give.
inventory_rules.name: findings

inventory_rules._comment: The number-word alternation ran to `ten` while the directory count stood at thirteen, so the rule could not have read a spelled-out true count even where one was written. `specs/*/harness/README.md` is in scope because that is where VERDICT.md sent the claim on 2026-08-03 when it re-stated FR-016 without a fixed count: `harness/` is the authority for how many there are. Widening the words to twenty and the scope to the harness index changed no firing count anywhere in the corpus — measured 2026-08-10, both readings zero in scope and one out of it — because the site the rule now reads was written in the same pass.
inventory_rules.name: committed-harnesses

inventory_rules._comment: The only rule in this set whose subject is not committed. `examples/` is git-ignored at `.gitignore:156`, so no checkout contains it and this rule reads nothing in CI by construction rather than by fault — measured across every run whose gate step executed, it has never once compared a claim. `precondition` is what makes that legible: with the declared path absent the skip says the rule is out of scope here, and the word `disabled` is reserved for a glob that matched nothing while its precondition held, which is the state that is actually a defect. The rule is kept rather than retired because the claims it guards are live and do rot, and it is not converted to a committed manifest because a manifest would check prose against a second copy of the prose instead of against the directories.
inventory_rules.name: vendored-repos

precondition.why: `examples/` is git-ignored at `.gitignore:156`; this rule reads a claim only in a working tree that has the vendored repositories checked out beside the corpus

_comment_definition_counts: Prose claims about how many members of a register a *specification* defines — '58 functional requirements'. The sibling of inventory_rules, and the difference is where the truth comes from: an inventory rule counts files against a glob, this one counts identifier definitions inside one document, using the same definition rule `identifier-resolution` uses. `namespace` names which identifier_namespaces entry the claim is about; the target is the `definition_count_target` sitting in the claiming document's own `specs/<feature>/` directory, which is how a plan or a tasks file finds the spec it quotes. Scoping matters for the same reason it does for inventory: these words in a research document are prose, not a count of a register. A target yielding zero definitions is an ERROR rather than a comparison, because zero is what a blind extractor returns and it also matches a claim of zero.
_comment_count_range: count-versus-range: a register's stated size beside a range of its own identifiers. The noun is the scope control — dropping it to a bare 'decisions' admits the struck-chain site in docs/spec-kit-workflow.md.
_comment_lifecycle_taxonomy: The session lifecycle's declared terminal states against the closed set FR-006 requires, which lives in Python rather than in markdown. Unlike every other check here, one side of this comparison is source: `lifecycle_taxonomy_source` is read from the corpus root and parsed with `ast` rather than imported, because --root may point at a fixture tree and a corpus checker that executes what it checks has a failure mode no regex does. The document side is a table rather than the fenced diagram it replaced — `~~` renders literally inside a fence, so a superseded member could not be struck in the house style, and a picture cannot say which members are owed. Both sides can degrade to the empty set and two empty sets reconcile perfectly, so zero parsed members is an error and zero table rows in a corpus that has the documents is an error too. See OD-26 and finding 027.
_comment_preserved_evidence: Bytes-level attestation over trees of preserved evidence — dated records of runs that already happened, which OD-31 rules are kept rather than rewritten. `attestation` is a witness held OUTSIDE `tree`, because a digest stored beside the bytes it covers is the self-report that let an E8->E19 rewrite through every green gate. `attestation_sha256` pins the witness's own bytes and is the half a human ratifies: `tools/check_corpus.py --reattest` writes the record and prints this digest, and never writes it here. That split is the mechanism — an attestation a tool can refresh attests nothing — so wiring a rebuild into anything that edits these artifacts, `neutralise_decision.py` above all, reproduces the vacuity one layer down. Scope is keyed on `root.marker`, a path each unit declares and which is neither its `tree` nor its `attestation`. Two earlier keyings were each defeated by the thing they were keyed on going missing. Keyed on `tree`, deleting the protected directory took the check to `skipped` while it announced itself disabled; an absent `tree` is now the `removed` violation, confirmed for each unit by deleting it. Keyed on `attestation`, a unit whose witness was missing or whose path was mis-typed was dropped from the run and reported nothing — `0 error(s), 0 warning(s)` with no skip line, which is also what a fully attested tree prints — so the guard reproduced, one layer up and inside itself, the silent-attestation failure it was built to close. A declared marker separates the two states the filter had merged: marker present and witness absent is `malformed`, and marker absent is a unit belonging to another root. That is also what lets the two fixture corpora and this repository share one list, and it is what a mis-typed `attestation` now fails on rather than passing through.

root.why: The harness this evidence belongs to. It holds live experiment code beside the two attested trees, so it survives the deletion of either of them and an absent `tree` stays a `removed` violation rather than going out of scope.

units.name: verifier-vs-judge-adjudication
units._why: The blind adjudication study, preserved on the same OD-31 ruling as the run directories beside it and attested as a SECOND unit rather than folded into the first. One unit per tree is what keeps a correction's blast radius equal to its subject: with the two trees merged under one pin, ratifying a correction to a run directory would also ratify, in the same digest and without saying so, whatever had moved under this tree in the same window. Split, the pins are independent, so the ratifier is told which body of evidence changed. Corrected 2026-08-11: an earlier form of this sentence credited that to `--reattest` printing `the pinned digest already matches; nothing to ratify` for the tree that did not move. That line could not fire on a plain rebuild — `generation` sits inside the digested document and `attest.build` moves it every time — and since `f7ade9f` it no longer carries those words. What a rebuild prints for the unmoved tree is `the attested tree has not moved since the ratified attestation`, compared on `tree_sha256`; the moved tree prints no corresponding line, so it is identified by that absence. The conclusion is untouched by the correction: pin independence predates the repair, and it discriminates provided the correction names its `--unit`. The house strike form is unavailable here — `~~` renders nowhere and this field is read as data — so the superseded form is named in prose instead, as the `inventory-count` comment above does. `tools/README.md` carries the long form. The merge is also unavailable mechanically: `attest.measure` walks one tree recursively and unfiltered on purpose, so a single unit spanning both would have to be rooted at `verifier-vs-judge/`, sweeping in the live harness that legitimately changes.

root.why: The same harness as the unit above, and the same reasoning: it is neither of the attested trees, so losing one of them is reported rather than tolerated.
The known-good corpus is the only root that carries this directory, which is what takes this unit out of scope in the other two without anything having to be absent by accident.
Present in the known-bad corpus alone.

units.name: fixture-unratified
units._why: The pin below is deliberately not the digest of that attestation. It is the state a rebuild leaves behind, and this unit is the only thing holding the rule that a rebuild does not clear the gate on its own.

root.why: Present in the known-bad corpus alone.

units.name: fixture-malformed
units._why: The pin below DOES match its attestation, and the tree matches too. What fails is the attestation's own internal arithmetic, so this unit holds the rule that a summary is reconciled against the entries beneath it rather than trusted.

root.why: Present in the known-bad corpus alone.

units.name: fixture-treegone
units._why: This unit's attestation is intact, ratified and self-consistent, and the tree it attests does not exist. It reports the loss once against the tree rather than once per attested file. A probe on 2026-08-11 stubbed each branch of attest.verify in turn and found this the only one the other four fixtures left standing, so it is fixtured here rather than trusted.

root.why: Present in the known-bad corpus alone. The marker is the unit's own directory rather than its `tree`, which is the point of this fixture: the tree is absent and the unit stays in scope.

units.name: fixture-witnessgone
units._why: The unit whose witness is absent, and the fixture for the failure kind this schema exists to make visible. Before the `root` marker, a unit whose `attestation` was missing or mis-typed was dropped by the scope filter and reported nothing at all: `--check preserved-evidence` printed `0 error(s), 0 warning(s)` and no skip line, which is what a fully attested tree prints. That is the class this check was built to close, reproduced inside the check. This unit declares a root that is present, so it is judged rather than filtered, and the `malformed` branch of `attest.verify` that reports a missing attestation is reachable from the check for the first time. There is no `attestation_sha256` because there are no bytes to pin.

root.why: Present in the known-bad corpus alone. The directory holds the attested `records/` tree and no attestation, so the marker survives in git while the witness it should sit beside does not exist.
